candidate_title: A pyramid recurrent network for predicting crowdsourced speech-quality ratings of real-world signals

review_output.decision_rationale: Stage 2 criteria require explicit preference-learning signals (ranking or A/B comparisons or an RL training loop) within the audio domain. The candidate paper focuses on predicting mean opinion scores (MOS) for real-world speech signals and uses MOS-based subjective ratings (e.g., MUSHRA-like procedures) rather than explicit ranking, A/B comparisons, or a learning loop driven by user preferences. Therefore it does not meet the Stage 2 inclusion criteria for preference-learning in audio. Supporting evidence: the text describes MOS prediction and encoder/decoder architecture for predicting MOS, not ranking-based preference learning.

refute_spans.quote: The proposed model predicts mean opinion scores of real-world signals using a novel deep-learning framework.

The encoder utilizes a stacked pyramid bidirectional long short term memory (pBLSTM) network, which has been successfully used in similar speech tasks (ASR [31] and voice conversion [39]), but not for speech assessment.

evidence_ledger.quote: The proposed model predicts mean opinion scores of real-world signals using a novel deep-learning framework.

candidate_title: Step-Audio: Unified Understanding and Generation in Intelligent Speech Interaction

review_output.decision_rationale: Stage 2 analysis finds explicit preference-learning signals in the Step-Audio paper (RLHF-based training for AQTA, explicit preference data construction, and a learning loop using Bradley-Terry/PPO). The work is audio-domain (real-time speech interaction) and is not a survey/review. Therefore it meets Stage 2 inclusion criteria and should be routed to formal Stage-2 consideration as include.

The reward model training initializes from a SFT model and proceeds through the two-stage training using the Bradley-Terry loss.

candidate_title: A differentiable perceptual audio metric learned from just noticeable differences

review_output.decision_rationale: Stage 2 canonical criteria are met: (1) the paper concerns preference learning via AB-style pairwise consideration of audio (two recordings are compared), (2) it is applied within the audio domain, and (3) it is not a survey. The work collects AB-type judgments between two audio signals and learns a differentiable perceptual metric from human judgments, demonstrating a learning component rather than evaluation-only. These attributes align with the Stage 2 inclusion criteria and are not contradicted by the provided evidence.
